objections.claim: Item 5.2 success_check states '`decreases` as more messages are sent. If it stays at 0% or fixed at 100%, FAIL'
objections.problem: 'Decreases' is directional but not threshold-bound. If the % drops from 100% to 99% across one large message, is that pass? A 1% delta inside the noise floor is not strong enough evidence that the meter is wired to a real token counter — it could be a placeholder constant tick. Falsifiability is borderline.
objections.required_evidence: Tighten success_check to: 'After the seed-style large paste, the percentage shown is non-zero AND non-100, AND the displayed delta from session-start to post-paste is at least 5 percentage points (i.e., consistent with a non-trivial fraction of a 1M-token budget consumed by a multi-thousand-token paste).' This makes a placeholder constant fail and a real counter pass.

objections.claim: Item 5.5 interaction step says 'toggle any sidebar / split-view / inspector control that changes the top-bar's content area width'
objections.problem: This is the only vague step in the plan. 'Any toggle' invites QA to skip if no obvious toggle exists. The user's spec for §5.5 is literally '没有自适应的另外一个案例' (another non-adaptive case), so the second case must actually be exercised — not skipped because QA couldn't find a toggle.
objections.required_evidence: BA should enumerate at least 2 concrete toggles QA must try (e.g., (a) collapse/expand the left sidebar via the hamburger button at the top-left; (b) switch between desktop and mobile viewports while staying in the same session), and require QA to record top-bar geometry before AND after each toggle. If neither toggle changes top-bar layout, capture that fact as evidence rather than treating §5.5 as 'no repro available'.

objections.claim: Item 5.12 says 'try 200MB or whatever exceeds the documented limit — if no limit known, try 200MB'
objections.problem: The documented limit is not stated anywhere in the BA spec. QA may waste time uploading a 200MB file via Playwright (which is slow and possibly unreliable) when a smaller threshold would suffice. Also, 'whatever exceeds the documented limit' is not falsifiable — QA doesn't know the limit.
objections.required_evidence: BA should either (a) name the documented attachment size limit (look it up in happy-app source, e.g., compose component or upload helper), or (b) instruct QA to first probe the limit via UI feedback (start at 10MB, escalate by 10x) and report the discovered ceiling. Without this, the oversize-error check is a guessing game.

objections.claim: Item 5.10 success_check: 'After reconnect, the visible message order is causal: either the long-task completion arrives first then the 2+2 answer, or just the 2+2 answer (if long task was discarded).'
objections.problem: The user's verbatim complaint in §5.10 is specifically about the BUG ordering: long-task self-reply arriving AFTER user sends '2+2' but BEFORE the '2+2' answer. The success_check correctly names the FAIL case but the PASS criterion 'or just the 2+2 answer (if long task was discarded)' is too lenient — it allows the renderer to swallow the entire long-task output and still pass. The user's spec also requires 'reconnect must be proactive (not user-action-triggered)', which the success_check does not test.
objections.required_evidence: Add an explicit check that the reconnect happens BEFORE the user sends '2+2' (e.g., observe WebSocket reconnection in dev-tools Network tab during the 2-minute idle window with no user action). Without that, even a passing message-order check would not satisfy acceptance point 1 ('proactive reconnect').

objections.claim: Test Session Plan step 6: 'Pick working directory /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev (the cloned monorepo)'
objections.problem: The active overnight worktree is at /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/.claude/worktrees/overnight-20260329-9ae57c91 (per git status). Spawning a Claude session against /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev itself, while another claude is running in the worktree, may cause Claude SDK file-watching contention. Not necessarily fatal, but worth flagging.
objections.required_evidence: Either (a) confirm /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev is safe to use as a Claude working directory while the orchestrator runs in the same tree, or (b) recommend an alternative directory like /tmp/dev-verify-13502 (mkdir + git clone or just an empty dir — Claude can read /etc, /usr/share, anything that gives it 'something to look at').

objections.claim: BA test session plan does not provision a fallback for the case where the dev daemon (pid 275490, port 35607) is NOT running by the time QA starts
objections.problem: BA assumes daemon is healthy. If the daemon has died/restarted between BA writing this spec and QA executing it, session creation will fail with no machine available. QA would have to abort with no recovery path stated.
objections.required_evidence: BA should add a precondition check at top of the QA hand-off: 'Before starting, verify dev daemon is reachable: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35607/state. If unreachable, restart via systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev.service (or escalate to user). Do NOT proceed to session creation if no machine is online in the dev account.'

objections.claim: QA handoff requires 'Per-item Section 4 entry' and a 'Section 4 patch unified across 13 entries'
objections.problem: The Section 4 entry format is referenced ('existing Section 4 format used in cycles 1–3') but never shown in the BA spec or context JSON. QA has to read Section 4 of the 349KB monolith spec to discover the format. This adds friction and introduces format-drift risk.
objections.required_evidence: BA should paste a sample Section 4 entry (e.g., one cycle-3 PASS-WITH-WARNING entry verbatim) into the QA hand-off contract as a template. Otherwise QA may produce a structurally-incompatible patch that the orchestrator has to fix.

summary: BA spec is thorough on scope, viewport coverage, falsifiability, and forbidden-pattern guards. 7 soft objections raised on per-item precision (5.2/5.5/5.10/5.12 success-check tightening), session-plan robustness (working-dir contention, daemon precondition), and handoff template completeness. None are hard rejects — BA can close any of them with a small revision OR QA can exercise judgement and document deviations.
items_with_concerns: 5.2: 'decreases' threshold not bounded; could pass on a placeholder 1% tick
5.5: 'toggle any control' is vague; needs at least 2 concrete toggle paths enumerated
5.10: PASS branch 'just the 2+2 answer' too lenient; proactive-reconnect acceptance point not directly tested
5.12: oversize-upload threshold not specified; 200MB is a fallback guess
